note: Birnbaum et al. alone described 13 affected individuals across 8 Ashkenazi Jewish families, which together with 2 siblings in Turkyilmaz et al. exceeds 10 patients.

evidence.text: Birnbaum et al. identified SGSM3 variants in 13 index cases/patients across families of Ashkenazi Jewish origin, and Turkyilmaz et al. identified a homozygous variant in two additional siblings, bringing the documented cohort to at least 15 affected individuals rather than fewer than 10.

source.title: A Strong Candidate Gene for Nonsyndromic Intellectual Disability Phenotype: SGSM3
source.quote: In all 13 index cases, the SGSM3 gene included … In this study, a novel homozygous stop-gain (NM_015705.6: c.1576C>T: p.(Arg526Ter)) variation was detected in the SGSM3 gene in two siblings with short stature and ID findings.

numbers.metric: Ashkenazi Jewish index cases reported by Birnbaum et al.
